$comment: Gateway configuration for the azd deployment path. Copy this file, fill in every
Without it the deployment produces an API Management instance containing only the
stock echo-api: no workload API, no named values and no llm-token-limit. The
gateway bills for its tier and governs nothing (ADR-007).
The authoritative schema is the gatewayServiceConfiguration definition in
environments/schema.json, and the Bicep type is gatewayConfiguration in
modules/api-management/types.bicep. Unknown keys are silently dropped by the
orchestrator, so check spelling against those two files.
This file is an example and is not read by any deployment.
$comment_audience: Application ID URI of the Entra app registration that represents this gateway.
Callers request a token for this audience. This is NOT a GUID and NOT the
caller's object ID - it is the identifier URI, for example api://<app-id>.
$comment_subnet: Must match the subnet the landing zone creates, unless you are deploying into a
prepared spoke whose subnet you own. The default prefix is main.bicep's
apiManagementSubnetPrefix. Preflight validates this prefix for overlap and
containment, so a wrong value is caught before the 30-minute gateway create.
$comment_dns: Service-scoped private DNS zone for <apim-name>.azure-api.net. NOT a
privatelink.azure-api.net zone: a classic injected instance cannot hold a
private endpoint, and Azure forbids a private zone for the shared apex domain.
$comment_stop: Emergency stop. true makes the gateway refuse new requests without a
redeployment. Leave false for a normal deployment.
$comment_streaming: ADR-004. Streaming is refused by default. When streaming is enabled the
llm-token-limit policy ALWAYS estimates prompt and completion tokens, with no
setting that changes it, so a streaming caller is enforced on estimates rather
than on billed usage. Enable only where that trade-off is recorded and accepted.
$comment_calls: Gateway-wide call-rate backstop in calls per minute, for callers that do not set
their own callsPerMinute. Token limits bound consumption but only after tokens
are counted; this bounds request volume. Omit to use the module default of 600.
$comment_token_defaults: Gateway-wide token limits, used for any caller that does not set its own.
Omit all three and the module defaults apply: 10000 TPM, 5000000 tokens Monthly.
Microsoft publishes no default for llm-token-limit - the policy reference lists
these with Default = N/A - so these numbers are ours, not vendor guidance.
10000 assumes roughly four callers sharing the default 'chat' deployment, which
ships at capacity 40 (Learn: 1 unit = 1,000 TPM for chat-class models, moved in
1,000 increments). Change the model or the capacity and you should revisit this.
1. These also cap each request. The gateway refuses any request whose
403 gateway_request_rejected / invalid-output-limit. With the defaults that
ceiling is 10000. Set tokensPerMinute too low and callers get a 403 that
looks like a permissions problem but is really a quota one.
2. Per-caller limits do not add up to a shared budget. Four callers at 10000 TPM
admit 40000 TPM of demand against ONE model deployment. If that exceeds the
TPM assigned to the deployment, the model refuses the excess instead of the
gateway, and the caller gets a backend error with nothing actionable in it.
Deploy-AilzIntegrated.ps1 warns when the sum looks oversubscribed.
$comment_callers: At least one entry is required. There is no unlimited path: a caller whose
object ID is not listed here is refused with 403 gateway_forbidden.
Only objectId, project and models are required - the token fields fall back to
the gateway defaults above, then to the module defaults. Set them per caller
only where one caller genuinely needs different limits from the rest.
objectId is the Entra OBJECT ID (a GUID) of the service principal, managed
identity or group that calls the gateway - find it with:
az ad sp show --id <app-id> --query id -o tsv
models must name deployed model deployment names, not model family names.
label is an optional readable billing dimension; without it the raw object ID
appears in cost telemetry. Keep distinct labels under 100.
